title: Periapical healing: 7 prognostic factors
topic: The seven factors Cohen's ch. 17 lists as having a major impact on periapical healing after nonsurgical RCT, each with its favorable state.

claims.claim: 1 · Periapical lesion: presence, size · better healing associated with: none, or smaller
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 1; Figs. 17.20, 17.21: pooled OR 2.4 for no radiolucency, 2.2 for small vs large). Cross-check: Ng, Mann & Gulabivala, Int Endod J 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626), abstract

claims.claim: 2 · Patency at the canal terminus · achieved
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 2: achieving patency increased the chance of success twofold, citing Ng 2011). Cross-check: Ng et al., Int Endod J 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626), abstract

claims.claim: 3 · Apical extent of preparation · flush · flush: root filling 0–2 mm within the radiographic apex
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 3 names the extent of chemomechanical preparation and cites Fig. 17.22, which pools root fillings: underextended 0.76, flush 0.81, overextended 0.66 probability of periapical health; flush is the root-filling category 0–2 mm within the radiographic apex; the text says canals are normally filled to the extent of preparation). Cross-check: Ng et al., Int Endod J 2008;41:6-31 (PMID 17931388) and 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626), abstracts

claims.claim: 4 · Intraoperative culture test · negative · a prognostic factor, though not routine practice
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 4; Fig. 17.19: pooled OR 2.1 for a negative preobturation culture; text: the practice has fallen out of clinical favor). Cross-check: Sjögren et al., Int Endod J 1997;30:297-306 (PMID 9477818), abstract

Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 5: if present, reduces the odds of success by 30%, citing Ng 2011). Cross-check: Ng et al., Int Endod J 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626), abstract (perforation P = 0.06)

claims.claim: 6 · Root-filling quality on radiograph · good, no voids
claims.source: Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 6; Fig. 17.23: pooled OR 3.9 for good-quality vs suboptimal root filling; the chapter says the criteria were not well defined; unsatisfactory = inadequate seal, poor apical seal or radiographic voids). Cross-check: Ng et al., Int Endod J 2008;41:6-31 (PMID 17931388), abstract

Ng & Gulabivala, Evaluation of Outcomes, ch. 17 in Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.: Summary of Factors Influencing Periapical Healing Following Nonsurgical Root Canal Treatment (bullet 7; Fig. 17.24: pooled OR 1.9 for satisfactory vs unsatisfactory restoration; good quality regardless of type). Cross-check: Ng et al., Int Endod J 2008;41:6-31 (PMID 17931388) and 2011;44:583-609 (PMID 21366626), abstracts

caption:
7 factors that influence periapical healing after nonsurgical root canal treatment: a study summary of the outcomes chapter in Cohen's.
Better healing is associated with: no periapical lesion (or a smaller one) · patency at the canal terminus · flush apical extent of preparation (pooled as root fillings 0–2 mm within the radiographic apex) · negative culture · no perforation · good root filling on radiograph · good coronal restoration.
Culture is prognostic, though not routine practice. Healing, not tooth survival. Associations, not causation. Schematic icons.
Ref: Ng & Gulabivala, ch. 17, Cohen's Pathways of the Pulp, 12th ed.
